questions.stem: Where does most nutrient absorption take place?
questions.explanation: Most nutrient absorption occurs in the small intestine, specifically in the ileum, which has a very large surface area due to villi and microvilli.

options.text: Finger-like projections on the inner wall of the small intestine that increase surface area

questions.explanation: Villi are tiny finger-like projections that line the inner wall of the small intestine. They greatly increase the surface area available for absorption of digested nutrients.

questions.stem: How are villi adapted for efficient absorption?

options.text: They are made of muscle tissue
They have a large surface area, thin walls (one cell thick), good blood supply, and contain lacteals

questions.explanation: Villi are adapted for absorption by having a large surface area, walls only one cell thick for short diffusion distance, a dense network of blood capillaries, and lacteals for absorbing fats.

questions.stem: How are fatty acids and glycerol absorbed?

options.text: They are absorbed into lacteals in the villi and transported via the lymphatic system
They are not absorbed at all
They pass through the stomach wall

questions.explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol are absorbed into the lacteals (lymph vessels) inside the villi and transported via the lymphatic system, eventually entering the blood.

questions.stem: By which process is glucose absorbed from the small intestine into the blood?
questions.explanation: Glucose is absorbed by a combination of diffusion (when concentration is higher in the gut) and active transport (to ensure all glucose is absorbed even against its concentration gradient).

questions.stem: What is the function of microvilli on the surface of villi?

options.text: To further increase the surface area for absorption
To move food along the intestine

questions.explanation: Microvilli are even smaller projections on the surface of the epithelial cells of villi. They further increase the surface area, forming a 'brush border' that maximises absorption.

questions.stem: What is absorbed in the large intestine?
questions.explanation: The large intestine mainly absorbs water from the remaining undigested material, along with some minerals and vitamins. This helps form solid faeces.
